sample_unit: LLM responses (382 unique prompts x 3 models)

links.outcome: Inappropriate LLM responses identified through multidisciplinary red-teaming of clinical scenarios
links.effect: 19.8% of 1146 responses labeled inappropriate; GPT-3.5 25.7%, GPT-4.0 16.2%, GPT-4.0 with internet 17.5%. Red teaming with 80 experts surfaced safety, privacy, hallucination, and bias failures.
links.quote: Results demonstrate a significant proportion of inappropriate responses across GPT-3.5, GPT-4.0, and GPT-4.0 with Internet (25.7%, 16.2%, and 17.5%, respectively) and illustrate the valuable role that non-technical clinicians can play in evaluating models.

links.outcome: Responses appropriate in older model but inappropriate in updated models
links.effect: 11.8% of responses were appropriate with GPT-3.5 but inappropriate in updated models.
links.quote: Interestingly, 11.8% of responses were deemed appropriate with GPT-3.5 but inappropriate in updated models, highlighting the ongoing need to evaluate evolving LLMs.

screen.reason: Empirical study using an expert red-teaming exercise to evaluate safety, privacy, hallucinations, and bias of LLMs across clinical scenarios.

primary.practice: expert red teaming / safety stress testing
